# NGINX — load-balancer-sse

Two backends balanced by an NGINX upstream with sticky sessions via a ROUTEID cookie, PUSH over Server-Sent Events. Affinity has to cover the EventSource GET and the separate client-to-server XHR POSTs.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

NGINX template (`nginx/http/load-balancer-sse/default.conf.template`):

```nginx
# SSE-only load balancer. Sticky sessions matter more here than with WebSocket:
# SSE is two separate connections — the EventSource GET that streams down and
# the XHR POSTs that go up — so both have to land on the backend that owns the
# session, not just one long-lived socket.

upstream application_balancer {
    server vaadin-1:8080;
    server vaadin-2:8080;

    # Sticky sessions via a cookie. The `sticky` directive is available in
    # open-source nginx since 1.29.6 (previously commercial-only), so it can
    # replace the coarser ip_hash balancing.
    sticky cookie ROUTEID path=/ httponly;
}

# Compression on, the way a real deployment has it — but never over a streamed
# response: text/event-stream (SSE push) and text/plain (streaming and long
# polling) are deliberately absent from gzip_types. text/html is always
# compressed and cannot be taken off the list.
gzip              on;
gzip_proxied      any;
gzip_types        text/css application/javascript application/json
                  application/xml image/svg+xml;

server {

    listen       80;
    server_name  localhost;

    location / {
        proxy_set_header        Host $host;
        proxy_set_header        X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header        X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header        X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

        proxy_http_version      1.1;
        proxy_buffering         off;
        proxy_read_timeout      300s;

        proxy_pass http://application_balancer/;
        proxy_redirect $scheme://$host/ $scheme://$http_host/;
    }
}
```
